description: The line plot titled “Finetuning for different r, Gazeta” illustrates the performance of four different model configurations on the ROUGE-1 metric as a function of log r, where r is a hyperparameter likely related to the rank or scaling of the adapter in LoRA or AdaLoRA fine-tuning methods. The x-axis, labeled “log r”, spans from 0 to 9 with integer tick marks at every 1 unit, indicating a linear scale of the logarithm of r. The y-axis, labeled “ROUGE-1”, ranges from 0 to 35 with major gridlines every 5 units, representing the summarization quality score. Four distinct lines are plotted: “T5 + LoRA” (red circles, solid line) starts at ~23.5 at log r = 0, rises slightly to ~24.5 by log r = 4, then plateaus near 24.5 through log r = 9. “MBart + LoRA” (blue circles, solid line) begins at ~5 at log r = 0, dips to ~2.5 at log r = 2, then sharply increases to ~19 at log r = 4, and continues rising to ~23.5 at log r = 8 before slightly declining to ~23 at log r = 9. “T5 + AdaLoRA” (green circles, solid line) starts at ~23.5, steadily increases to ~27 at log r = 4, then gradually climbs to ~30 by log r = 6 and plateaus near 30 through log r = 9. “MBart + AdaLoRA” (orange circles, solid line) begins at ~5, rises to ~9 at log r = 1, ~13.5 at log r = 2, ~19.5 at log r = 3, then jumps to ~32 at log r = 4, and continues to climb slightly to ~33.5 by log r = 6, remaining flat through log r = 9. All lines use circular markers and solid lines, with no error bars or shading. The plot suggests that AdaLoRA generally outperforms LoRA, especially for MBart, and that performance tends to saturate at higher log r values.
